what_its_for: Eliglustat is used to treat adults with Gaucher disease type 1. This is a rare inherited condition where a fatty substance builds up in organs like your liver, spleen, and bone marrow. This medicine helps reduce that buildup and can improve symptoms such as an enlarged liver or spleen, low blood counts, and bone problems.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsule. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep an even amount of medicine in your body. Your doctor will determine the right dose for you based on how your body processes this medication (called your CYP2D6 metabolizer status), which is determined by a genetic test before you start treatment.
dosing: The usual dose is either one 84 mg capsule taken twice daily (morning and evening) or one 84 mg capsule taken once daily, depending on your genetic test results and other medicines you take. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is not too close to your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store eliglustat at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from moisture and heat. Store it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a safe drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your body to unsafe levels. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, because many medications can interact with eliglustat. Avoid starting any new medicines without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: irregular or fast heartbeat, dizziness or fainting, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness or weakness, shortness of breath, or chest pain. Also contact your doctor if you notice any new or worsening symptoms, experience side effects that bother you, become pregnant or plan to become pregnant, or start or stop taking any other medications.
when_it_works: Eliglustat is a long-term treatment and works gradually over time. Most patients start to see improvements in symptoms like reduced organ size and improved blood counts within 6 to 12 months. It is important to keep taking it every day as directed, even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may harm an unborn baby. Effective birth control is recommended during treatment. It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Kidney or liver problems: Eliglustat is not recommended for patients with moderate or severe liver problems or certain kidney conditions — your doctor will decide if this medicine is safe for you. Children: This medicine is only approved for adults. Elderly: Older adults may need extra monitoring while taking this medicine.
